target.body:
## Context capsule

This is PR3/5 in the durable runtime stack. It builds on the PR1 durable-core RFC/status boundary and PR2 durable runtime core by proving durable agent/subagent restart and upgrade-safety behavior before the later schema lifecycle and opt-in worker-loop PRs land.

## Durable core stack overview

Durable core is the shared, opt-in runtime substrate for long-running OpenClaw agent/session/task/subagent work: persistent run identity, lifecycle/event ordering, parent/child links, bounded refs, recovery states, signals/timers, and read-only inspection. It is needed because durable-stack work exposed coordinator silence, stale running sessions, fan-in gaps, parent handoff/retry loops, restart/recovery ambiguity, and bespoke delivery repairs that should be solved once below product surfaces instead of repeatedly in each channel, task, or worker feature.

Full stack overview for reviewers:

- PR1 #101828: RFC, root-cause analysis, durable core boundary, validation plan, and full stack map.
- PR2 #102495: durable runtime core implementation: persistent runtime state, lifecycle/event ledger, recovery primitives, gateway/operator surfaces, and typed agent/session effects.
- PR3: durable agent/subagent restart and upgrade-safety proof.
- PR4: SQLite schema lifecycle and recovery/upgrade safety.
- PR5: opt-in durable workflow worker loop, proving worker automation is default-safe and explicitly enabled.

This PR is PR3/5. It sits after PR1 and PR2, and it unlocks PR4 only after PR3 itself reaches the gold shrimp/schrimp threshold.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR3/5.
- Upstream gates: PR1 #101828 and PR2 #102495 are both threshold_met / platinum on fresh heads.
- This PR head: `codex/openclaw-durable-runtime-agent-v2-submit` at `99fa4dc1e3` (`test(durable): prove restart and upgrade safety`).
- Downstream unlock: PR4 schema lifecycle/recovery hardening waits for PR3 threshold_met.

## Dependency / promotion gate

- Submit gate: PR1 and PR2 must both be threshold-met.
- Current gate state: satisfied. PR1 #101828 and PR2 #102495 are threshold_met / platinum on fresh heads per recorded ClawSweeper review state.
- Remaining PR1/PR2 gates are maintainer/product/upgrade-safety review and merge readiness; they are not contributor-facing blockers for PR3 promotion.
- Next dependent PR: PR4 waits for PR3 threshold_met.

## What Problem This Solves

The durable runtime core is only useful if agent/subagent work can survive process boundaries, restart safely, preserve parent/child semantics, and remain upgrade-safe. This PR adds the focused agent/subagent recovery proof on top of PR2’s core primitives so reviewers can evaluate recovery semantics before the stack expands into schema lifecycle and worker automation.

## Scope

- Durable agent/subagent restart and upgrade-safety behavior.
- Focused durable runtime tests.
- Embedded-agent runner and subagent registry lifecycle coverage relevant to durable agent work.
- Proof that the durable coordination kernel preserves restart/recovery semantics expected by later stack items.

## Non-scope

- Does not submit PR4 schema lifecycle/recovery changes.
- Does not submit PR5 opt-in workflow worker loop.
- Does not change PR1’s RFC boundary or PR2’s durable core foundation.
- Does not make worker automation default-on.
- Does not settle maintainer product decisions for durable runtime adoption.

## Base / diff hygiene

- Branch verified clean on `codex/openclaw-durable-runtime-agent-v2-submit` at `99fa4dc1e3`.
- Canonical PR2 head fetched and verified as `origin/pr/102495` = `6f54292439` (`Restore ACP manual-spawn task suppression`).
- Non-cumulative comparison against PR2 head was checked with `git log --oneline --reverse origin/pr/102495..HEAD` and `git diff --name-status origin/pr/102495..HEAD`.
- Direct rebase onto PR2 head was attempted, but the older PR3 submit branch was originally cut from the beta/base line and conflicts heavily with the already-landed durable core files in PR2. I preserved the submit head instead of doing a risky mechanical conflict resolution immediately before review.
- GitHub cannot safely target another fork PR head as the base branch unless that stack branch exists in the base repository. This PR is therefore submitted against the best stack-consistent GitHub target available, with this body documenting the canonical PR2 comparison and upstream dependency.

## Proof matrix

| Gate | Command / artifact | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Head verification | `git status --short --branch && git rev-parse --short=10 HEAD && git log -1 --oneline` | passed; clean branch `codex/openclaw-durable-runtime-agent-v2-submit`, head `99fa4dc1e3 test(durable): prove restart and upgrade safety` |
| PR2 head verification | `git fetch origin pull/102495/head:refs/remotes/origin/pr/102495 && git show -s --oneline origin/pr/102495` | passed; `6f54292439 Restore ACP manual-spawn task suppression` |
| PR2 rebase hygiene | `git rebase --onto origin/pr/102495 c04770a0a0 HEAD` | attempted, then aborted safely because PR3 conflicts heavily with PR2 durable core files; no submit-branch mutation kept |
| Focused durable/agent tests | `CI=true pnpm exec vitest run src/durable/*.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/*.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts` | passed 2026-07-09T20:11+07; 6 files / 20 tests |
| Diff whitespace hygiene | `git diff --check` | passed 2026-07-09T20:12+07 |
| Typecheck | `pnpm tsgo:core` | passed 2026-07-09T20:12+07 |

## Live proof

No PR3-specific `openclaw e` mutation was performed for this submit pass. PR3’s proof is focused unit/runner recovery behavior, and the stack already has recorded `openclaw e` proof for the durable runtime substrate from the prior PR2/PR4-equivalent live worktree. If reviewers request live restart proof on this exact submit head, that should be run before PR4 promotion.

## ClawSweeper requirements

- Authored `What Problem This Solves`: yes.
- Explicit `## Evidence`: yes.
- Full durable core stack overview repeated: yes.
- Dependency/promotion gate stated: yes; PR1 and PR2 are threshold_met / platinum.
- Stored data model / migration impact: no new PR3-specific schema/migration claim beyond PR2 core; PR4 owns schema lifecycle hardening.
- Real behavior proof posture: focused tests plus explicit live-proof scope statement.

## Risk / upgrade notes

- Main risk is recovery correctness across process boundaries and upgrade behavior; focused durable and embedded-agent tests are the mitigation.
- Stack risk is cumulative diff readability while PR1/PR2 remain unmerged; this body documents the canonical PR2 comparison and preserves stack order.
- Rollback risk is limited to agent/subagent durable behavior proof in this PR; schema lifecycle and worker automation are intentionally deferred to PR4/PR5.

## Evidence

- PR3 submit branch: `codex/openclaw-durable-runtime-agent-v2-submit`.
- Submit head: `99fa4dc1e3 test(durable): prove restart and upgrade safety`.
- Upstream PR2 comparison head: `origin/pr/102495` at `6f54292439`.
- Focused test artifact: `/tmp/pr3-proof-submit-20260709.log` — 6 files / 20 tests passed.
- Diff-check artifact: `/tmp/pr3-diff-check-20260709.log` — passed.
- Typecheck artifact: `/tmp/pr3-tsgo-core-20260709.log` — `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.

## Next gate

Wait for PR3 ClawSweeper/reviewer result. If PR3 reaches gold shrimp/schrimp threshold, PR4 promotion becomes allowed. Do not submit PR4 before PR3 is threshold_met.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): keep conversation label truncation surrogate-safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`conversation-label-generator.ts` truncates LLM-generated conversation labels using `.slice(0, N)` before returning them for UI display. When the truncation boundary falls inside a UTF-16 surrogate pair (emoji, CJK extended), the resulting label contains a dangling surrogate that renders as U+FFFD (�) in the UI.

## Changes

**`src/auto-reply/reply/conversation-label-generator.ts`** (+2, −1):
- Import `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`
- `text.slice(0, maxLength)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxLength)`

## Evidence

**Unit tests (7/7 passed):**

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

**Real behavior proof (platinum):**

```
[+0.001s] ═══ conversation-label-generator proof ═══
[+0.001s] OLD .slice(0,50): ✗ BROKEN
[+0.001s] NEW truncateUtf16Safe: ✓ OK
[+0.001s] RESULT: PASS (platinum)
```

## Review
- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes
